cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The player resolves each media entry to the circular buffers whose media index points at it and builds the pipeline from them; the texture and spatial-audio paths consume these buffers.

The player requires the extension on media-backed accessors only to warn when it is missing, reads the suggested update rate into the media buffer handler where it is assigned and never used, and registers the header buffer view that nothing consumes; the extension does not drive timed access.

cases.case: Sample format extracted from the accessor and passed to the MAF
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Component type, sample type, byte offset, stride and attribute type of each media accessor are converted to the MAF buffer description.

cases.case: Header configuration from MPEG_accessor_timed passed to the MAF
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The MAF buffer description carries no immutable flag or header presence; the player and the MAF both assume immutable headers, and the extension's immutable value is only checked for video textures, with a warning.

cases.case: Header presence taken from the bufferView attribute
cases.what: A bufferView value of 0 or more only copies the view into the configuration; header handling is not switched by it: the audio reader always uses accessor headers and the video texture path only warns when a bufferView is present.

cases.case: Overwrite accessor and bufferView info from the header
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The player does not overwrite accessor or buffer view values from a per-frame header: audio reads only the sample count and skips a fixed header length, and a video texture accessor with a header bufferView is only warned about.

cases.case: Audio delivered in the requested format
cases.what: Output format and channel count follow the buffer description, but audio resampling is switched off, so audio whose format, channel count or planarity differs from what the pipeline expects is not converted and is not played; only an exact match is delivered.

cases.case: Video delivered in the requested format
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The video decoder always converts to packed 24-bit RGB; the requested component type, sample type and plane layout in the buffer description are not read (a source comment marks this as to be done).

cases.case: Audio frames carry the timed accessor information header before the data
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. For audio the MAF writes a header per channel accessor at the start of each buffer frame and the samples follow it; it does so for every audio buffer, without regard to whether the scene signals a header.
Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The video decoder writes only pixel data into the buffer frame and never writes a header.

cases.case: Two bufferViews on a timed accessor
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Reference scenes give audio timed accessors both an accessor bufferView and a bufferView inside the extension, and the exporter writes both when headers are enabled.

cases.case: Accessor bufferView references the timed media data
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The accessor-level bufferView points at the 'MPEG_media.frame' view inside the circular buffer that receives the media.

cases.case: Extension bufferView points to the header
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Where the extension has a bufferView it refers to a view named for the timed accessor header, 32 bytes for a scalar float accessor, in the same buffer; the exporter sets that view's length from the header field layout but never sets its offset (a misspelled attribute), so with several headers in one buffer the views would not be placed apart.

cases.case: No extension bufferView means no header
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Video texture accessors omit the extension bufferView and no header view is reserved for them in the buffer; the exporter only adds a header view when headers are requested, which the video exporter does not do.

cases.case: Both bufferViews in the same buffer
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. In every reference scene with both views present they refer to the same buffer (checked for all scenes using the extension); the exporter builds the header view from the accessor view's buffer.

cases.case: Timed accessors point only to circular buffers
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Every timed accessor in the reference scenes refers through its bufferView to a buffer carrying the circular-buffer extension; the exporter creates the media buffer with that extension.
Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The extension appears only inside accessor objects in the scenes, and the exporter attaches it to accessors.
Rests on reading only; nothing was run. No reference scene sets immutable to false and the exporter never writes the flag, so a timed accessor whose type or component changes is not exercised.

cases.case: Extension bufferView buffer equals accessor buffer
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The header view and the accessor view name the same buffer in all scenes; the exporter copies the buffer from the accessor's view.

Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Accessors without an extension bufferView have no header view declared and none is reserved in the buffer layout, so the file is consistent with the assumption.

cases.case: immutable present and true when no header
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Timed accessors without an extension bufferView do not carry an immutable flag in any reference scene (the exporter never writes one), so the flag is not present as the sentence requires.
Rests on reading only; nothing was run. No scene or exporter code declares a header that changes (immutable false); only static-header configurations appear.

cases.case: access by frame index or timestamp

Rests on reading only; nothing was run. No circular buffer in any reference scene has a uri, and the exporter builds the buffer with uri unset.

Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The exporter sets the buffer length to the header sizes plus one frame's worth of accessor data, not multiplied by a frame count, and scenes that omit count (default 2) carry a length equal to a single padded frame (230400 x 4 bytes = 921600).

cases.case: one frame read per rendering cycle
cases.what: Reading only; nothing was run. The player's update runs every rendered frame and, for each buffer feeding a video texture, tries to read the frame due at the current time and uploads it.

cases.case: previous frame kept when no new frame
cases.what: reading only; nothing was run. The texture is updated only when a new frame is returned, so the earlier frame stays on the texture otherwise.

cases.case: buffer data has the declared format
cases.what: Reading only; nothing was run. The player passes the format attribute to the video texture but ignores it, interpreting every buffer as RGB24 (the code notes that format and YUV conversion are still to be done); the planar-YUV class exists but is never created.

cases.case: actual picture size passed to the renderer
cases.what: The player always uses the width and height from MPEG_texture_video and never reads a picture size from the buffer frame header, so the case where the decoder size differs is not handled; the player assumes the buffer is delivered at the declared size.

cases.case: fallback to raw reconstructed data without V3C support
cases.what: No V3C code exists, so the extension is ignored; each primitive attribute accessor in a media-backed buffer is mapped to a MAF attribute type and requested from the pipeline as a raw buffer, although the received data is not applied to a mesh.
The optional V3C reconstruction is not implemented.

requirements.name: AR Anchoring / MPEG_anchor extension

cases.what: The loader reads an MPEG_anchor reference on the scene, attaches every root node of the scene to the anchor's trackable and sets the anchor up.
The loader reads an MPEG_anchor reference on each node, attaches that node to the anchor's trackable and sets the anchor up.
MPEG_anchor is in the list of extensions the loader supports and has parsed schema classes for the root, scene and node objects.

noted: Anchor objects are only instantiated in Android builds (AddMPEGAnchor is compiled under UNITY_ANDROID); other platforms parse but do not anchor.

cases.case: Trackables and anchors read from the root extension
cases.what: The loader reads the trackables and anchors arrays from the glTF root MPEG_anchor extension and builds one trackable object and one anchor object per entry.
requiresAnchoring is a boolean on the parsed anchor, copied into the anchor instance and passed to the trackable at set-up.

cases.case: TRUE: assets hidden until the anchor pose is known (application, 2D and 3D marker, geo trackables)
cases.what: Application and Geo hide while unanchored, but Marker3D hides every frame and never assigns an anchor so the assets never appear, and the hide path for Marker2D is not completed when no anchor is tracked.

cases.case: TRUE: assets hidden until the anchor pose is known (floor, plane)
cases.what: For floor and plane trackables nothing deactivates the attached nodes before the first plane is found; the loader activates them at scene end, and they are only hidden again if a previously built anchor is lost.
The controller trackable never creates an anchor or pose, so with requiresAnchoring set its assets are never attached to a pose; the flag is stored but unused.
When the flag is false the trackables do not deactivate the attached nodes, which stay active and are parented to the anchor once it exists.

cases.case: Required space compared to estimated real-world bounds (floor, plane)
cases.what: minimumRequiredSpace is compared with the detected plane's bounding box (extended by a fixed 2.5 height) axis by axis, not as a volume.
Application, controller, viewer, marker and geo trackables store the required space but never compare it with an estimated space.
The aligned property is parsed as an enumeration with NOT_USED=0, ALIGNED_NOTSCALED=1, ALIGNED_SCALED=2 and defaults to NOT_USED.
The value is forwarded to the trackable, but every trackable ignores it (floor and plane have an empty method, others have it commented out), so no alignment or scaling is applied.
geometricConstraint is parsed as HORIZONTAL_PLANE=0 or VERTICAL_PLANE=1 and selects horizontal or vertical plane detection.
The geo trackable reads three floats from coordinates and uses them to create a geospatial anchor.

The first value is passed where the geospatial anchor call takes latitude and the second where it takes longitude; the reference geo scenes also list latitude first. This rests on reading only: the ARCore Extensions signature was not opened.

coordinates[0] is used as the latitude argument of the anchor call and no range or sign check is made on it, so a longitude in the first position is not interpreted as longitude. Rests on reading only.
coordinates[1] is used as the longitude argument of the anchor call and no range check is made, so a latitude in the second position is not interpreted as latitude. Rests on reading only.
coordinates[2] is passed unconverted as the altitude of the geospatial anchor; the datum is whatever that call uses (not opened), so this rests on reading only.
The controller trackable only stores the path; it computes no grip position or orientation and never provides a pose, so assets are never attached.

cases.case: Application trackable has a right-handed space
cases.what: The application trackable resolves an ARCore cloud anchor by its id and neither checks nor converts the handedness of the pose (reading only).

cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. When requiresAnchoring is false (the default) the trackables never deactivate attached assets, which are placed once the anchor exists and otherwise stay active.

Floor and Geometric compare the plane-boundary box (height fixed 2.5 m) per axis against minimumRequiredSpace and create no anchor when smaller, but the assets are not skipped because they were activated when the scene finished loading and nothing hides them (Geometric has no per-frame update).
Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Marker, viewer, application, geo-marker and controller trackables store the required space but never compare it with anything.

cases.what: The loader initialises the trackable, attaches the nodes and the actions are invoked once tracked, but Geometric sets only the node's world position and never parents it to the anchor at build time, and Floor overrides the rotation to face the camera, so assets are not placed in the anchor's local space.

Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Actions listed on the anchor are invoked once, when tracking is first reported; the transform action is declared but not executed because its Delay property is not implemented, and the haptic and avatar actions are likewise not executed.
